title: FIPS PUB 184: Integration Definition for Information Modeling (IDEF1X)
engineering_principles: Separates identifying, mandatory non-identifying and optional non-identifying relationships. Defines complete and incomplete category clusters. Requires non-specific relationships to be refined in the key-based phase.
practical_examples: Employee with salaried and hourly categories; project and task identifying relationship; robber and bank many-to-many resolution.
why_it_matters: The only full, freely readable formal specification of an ER-style notation found in this pass.
authority_rationale: Primary US federal standard text, read in full by pdftotext. Withdrawn, so authority is historical.
notes: A US government standard, not an ISO one, so resource_type is the closest enum value. Withdrawal date and the ISO/IEC/IEEE 31320-2:2012 successor come only from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IDEF1X (opened); no NIST withdrawal notice was opened.

title: Crow's Foot Notation
engineering_principles: Reports Everest's own explanation of the symbol as non-directional and showing manyness.
practical_examples: Footnote cites Computing Systems 1976, Proceedings Fifth Texas Conference on Computing Systems, Austin, TX, pages 39-46.
why_it_matters: Closest readable source for the origin of the notation; it quotes Everest by correspondence.
authority_rationale: Vendor blog carrying a personal communication; the 1976 paper itself was not opened.
notes: The vertabelo.com URL redirects here. Second source: https://runestone.academy/ns/books/published/practical_db/PART2_DATA_MODELING/04-other-notations/other-notations.html (opened), which attributes the family to Everest 1976 and explains maximum and minimum cardinality symbols. Body text and footnote name the venue differently.

title: Inheritance mapping patterns: Single Table, Class Table, Concrete Table Inheritance
engineering_principles: Names the three mapping patterns and the motive of each: fewer joins, clear mapping to objects, one row per object.
practical_examples: None on the public pages; they refer to Chapter 12 of the book.
why_it_matters: Common vocabulary for the three options.
authority_rationale: Well-known author, but public pages are short catalog summaries of Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture.
notes: Also opened: https://martinfowler.com/eaaCatalog/classTableInheritance.html and https://martinfowler.com/eaaCatalog/concreteTableInheritance.html. The book chapter was not read, so no detailed trade-offs are drawn from Fowler.

title: An Introduction to Hibernate 6: inheritance mapping and naming strategies
engineering_principles: Compares three strategies on query shape, NOT NULL, foreign keys and normalization.
practical_examples: Subclass columns cannot be NOT NULL under SINGLE_TABLE; associations to a superclass cannot have a foreign key under TABLE_PER_CLASS.
why_it_matters: The clearest readable constraint-level comparison found.
authority_rationale: Official project documentation, read directly.
notes: The user guide was also opened for naming strategy defaults: https://docs.hibernate.org/orm/6.6/userguide/html_single/ (the docs.jboss.org address redirects there).

title: EF Core: Inheritance
engineering_principles: TPH is the default and makes columns nullable as needed. The page states TPT often performs worse than TPH.
practical_examples: Blog and RssBlog mapped under all three strategies, with generated DDL.
why_it_matters: Vendor default and vendor performance statement for subtype storage.
authority_rationale: Official Microsoft documentation, read directly.
notes: The linked performance page with measured numbers was not opened.

title: EF Core: Many-to-many relationships
engineering_principles: A many-to-many cannot be represented with a simple foreign key and needs a join table.
practical_examples: Post and Tag with PostTag join table and generated schema.
why_it_matters: Shows how an ORM treats the join table as a real or hidden entity.
authority_rationale: Official Microsoft documentation, read directly.
notes: Read in part by keyword extraction.

title: SQL Server: Hierarchical data
engineering_principles: Compares hierarchyid with parent/child by operation and lists when parent/child is better.
practical_examples: Subtree queries are faster with hierarchyid; moving a parent/child row touches one row, against n rows for hierarchyid.
why_it_matters: The only vendor-written comparison of hierarchy designs found.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation, read directly; comparative statements have no numbers.
notes: PostgreSQL cycle handling in recursive queries: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/queries-with.html (opened). The PostgreSQL ltree page was downloaded but only its title was reviewed.

title: ISO/IEC FCD 11179-5 Naming and identification principles (2004 committee draft)
core_concepts: scope and authority of a convention
engineering_principles: A convention documents scope, authority, semantic, syntactic, lexical and uniqueness rules. The annex shows an object class, qualifier, property, representation ordering.
practical_examples: Cost Budget Period Total Amount; Employee Last Name; Tree Height Measure.
why_it_matters: First text of the 11179-5 rule structure read in this research; it goes beyond the scope statement.
authority_rationale: Committee document, not a published edition. Annex A is informative and the download was truncated.
notes: Download stopped at 143,828 bytes with 139,820 bytes missing. Extracted text reaches at least Annex A.4 and is incomplete. Do not cite as the published 2005 or 2015 edition.

title: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 32 Freely Available Standards
engineering_principles: Lists ISO/IEC 11179-5:2005 (2nd edition) among freely available SC 32 standards.
practical_examples: Table of editions, including 11179-1:2004 through 11179-6:2005.
why_it_matters: Indicates an older published edition of the naming part was released free.
authority_rationale: Committee's own page, but it lists superseded editions and links to the old ISO location.
notes: https://standards.iso.org/ittf/PubliclyAvailableStandards/index.html (opened) says the ITTF site is closed and deliverables are on the ISO and IEC webstores. The free copy itself was not obtained.

title: Active Record Basics
engineering_principles: Convention over configuration: singular class, plural snake_case table.
practical_examples: BookClub maps to book_clubs; foreign keys such as order_id.
why_it_matters: Primary evidence for the plural convention in a major framework.
authority_rationale: Official framework guide, read directly.

title: Django Model Meta options
engineering_principles: Table name is app label plus model class name, so it is singular by default.
practical_examples: App bookstore and class Book give bookstore_book.
why_it_matters: Primary evidence that a major framework defaults to singular with an app prefix.
authority_rationale: Official framework documentation, read directly.

title: EF Core: Indexes and constraints
engineering_principles: EF Core creates an index on foreign key properties by convention.
practical_examples: Default index name IX_<type name>_<property name>.
why_it_matters: Shows that foreign key indexing can be a framework default, not a lint rule.
authority_rationale: Official Microsoft documentation, read directly.
notes: Table naming: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ef/core/modeling/entity-types (opened). Pending model check: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ef/core/managing-schemas/migrations/managing (opened).

title: Prisma: Database mapping
engineering_principles: Decouples model names from table names. Says plural snake_case tables are common but recommends singular PascalCase models.
practical_examples: Model Comment mapped to table comments.
why_it_matters: A primary source that separates application naming from database naming.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation, read directly.
notes: The older /docs/orm/prisma-schema path redirected to a v7 path.

title: GitLab: Foreign keys and associations
engineering_principles: Requires an index for foreign keys, and accepts a composite index with the foreign key in first position.
practical_examples: Constraint naming: fk_<table name>_<column name>_<foreign table name>, for example fk_projects_group_id_groups.
why_it_matters: A public organization rule on foreign key indexes with the reason stated.
authority_rationale: Public engineering standards of a large PostgreSQL application; binding only inside GitLab.
notes: Naming page: https://docs.gitlab.com/development/database/constraint_naming_convention/ (opened). Tenant key detail: https://docs.gitlab.com/development/database/multiple_databases/ (opened) says the sharding key section moved; the new location was not opened.

title: Oracle Database 19c SQL Language Reference: Database Object Names and Qualifiers
engineering_principles: Nonquoted identifiers cannot be reserved words. Names reach 128 bytes under COMPATIBLE 12.2 or higher. Advises same names for same things across tables.
practical_examples: department_id used in both employees and departments; fin_ prefix for a FINANCE application.
why_it_matters: Corrects the gap note that no vendor prescribes naming beyond identifier rules, at least for Oracle.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation, read directly.
notes: Says nothing on singular or plural in the text read.

title: Schemalint
engineering_principles: Lints a live PostgreSQL catalog, with built-in rules and custom plugins.
practical_examples: Rule config such as name-inflection singular; missing index reports a suggested CREATE INDEX.
why_it_matters: Has built-in checks for foreign key indexes, primary keys, required columns and RLS.
authority_rationale: Project README and rule source read directly; community project.
notes: Rule source opened under https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kristiandupont/schemalint/main/src/rules/ (references.ts, requirePrimaryKey.ts, mandatoryColumns.ts, rowLevelSecurity.ts, types.ts, nameCasing.ts, nameInflection.ts). PostgreSQL only.

title: Squawk rules
engineering_principles: Focuses on statements that could block reads or writes or break clients.
practical_examples: adding-foreign-key-constraint recommends NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT.
why_it_matters: Defines the boundary: migration safety rather than schema design policy.
authority_rationale: Official tool documentation; rule list read, only a few rule pages opened.
notes: Also opened: https://squawkhq.com/docs/adding-foreign-key-constraint, https://squawkhq.com/docs/identifier-too-long, https://squawkhq.com/docs/prefer-identity.

title: SQLFluff: References rules
engineering_principles: RF04 flags keywords used as identifiers, with policy options for aliases and other identifiers.
practical_examples: Rule overview reports 79 rules in 11 categories.
why_it_matters: Only documented reserved-word style lint found, with a stated limit.
authority_rationale: Official tool documentation, read directly.
notes: Overview: https://docs.sqlfluff.com/en/stable/reference/rules/ (opened). Convention and capitalisation pages opened; aliasing, ambiguous, structure, layout and dialect pages not read.

title: Atlas: Migration analyzers
engineering_principles: Analyzers for naming and destructive changes. Custom rule language can assert schema conditions.
practical_examples: Documented rule examples: require-index-fk-columns, table-required-columns, id-column-required, ensure-row-security-enabled.
why_it_matters: Custom rule docs include a ready example for foreign key indexes and required columns.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation, read directly.
notes: Custom rule language: https://atlasgo.io/lint/rules (opened), stated to be available exclusively to Pro users.

title: Liquibase Secure custom policy checks
engineering_principles: Custom checks confirm specific syntax or objects are present in a changelog or database.
practical_examples: Check names TableColumnLimit and ObjectNameMustMatch appear in the checks run reference.
why_it_matters: Commercial option for governance checks.
authority_rationale: Official documentation, but the built-in check catalog could not be opened.
notes: Requires a Liquibase Secure license. Also opened: https://docs.liquibase.com/reference-guide/policy-check-and-flow-commands-and-parameters/checks-run (redirected) and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liquibase/custom_policychecks/main/README.md.

title: pgTAP documentation
engineering_principles: Assertion functions test named objects inside PostgreSQL.
practical_examples: SELECT has_pk( :table ); tables_are( :schema, :tables ).
why_it_matters: Assertion coverage for primary keys, foreign keys, column types and indexes.
authority_rationale: Official project documentation, read directly.
notes: Functions assert named objects; a schema-wide sweep would need generated tests, which is inference.

title: tSQLt: AssertEqualsTableSchema
engineering_principles: Compares table metadata against an expected table. FakeTable removes constraints from the object under test.
practical_examples: FakeTable page warns that a faked table does not test constraints.
why_it_matters: SQL Server test option, with a documented blind spot.
authority_rationale: Official documentation, read directly; user guide footer dates to 2020.
notes: Also opened: https://tsqlt.org/user-guide/ and https://tsqlt.org/user-guide/isolating-dependencies/faketable/.

title: utPLSQL expectations
engineering_principles: General purpose PL/SQL test framework based on annotations and expectations.
practical_examples: Documentation example counts rows in a named table and expects zero.
why_it_matters: Oracle test option; no schema-specific assertion found.
authority_rationale: Official documentation, read directly.
notes: Home page also opened: https://www.utplsql.org/utPLSQL/latest/.

title: prisma-lint rules
engineering_principles: Lints Prisma schema files, not the database.
practical_examples: tenantId is used in the rule examples for field-order and ignore comments.
why_it_matters: Only source found whose own examples use a tenant key.
authority_rationale: Third-party open source project, rules file read directly. Not a Prisma product.
notes: README also opened.

title: Testcontainers: Getting started
engineering_principles: Tests run against real services in Docker, without mocks or in-memory services.
practical_examples: PostgreSQL module examples across languages at https://testcontainers.com/modules/postgresql/.
why_it_matters: Replaces the definition gap recorded in research_gaps.md.
authority_rationale: Official project site, read directly.
notes: Infrastructure only: it runs checks but performs none.

title: DAMA-DMBOK
engineering_principles: Describes itself as not a prescriptive standard, not a regulation and not exhaustive.
practical_examples: Publisher pages sell print and PDF formats.
why_it_matters: Settles the status question: DMBOK is a reference, so it cannot be cited as a binding rule.
authority_rationale: Publisher's own page, read directly; book content remains unread.
notes: Also opened: https://dama.org/about-dama/what-is-data-management/ (states 11 knowledge areas, names only 6), https://dama.org/dama-dmbok2-revised-edition-faqs/ (April 2024 availability), https://dama.org/dama-dmbok-3-0-project/, https://technicspub.com/dmbok2/.

title: DCAM
engineering_principles: Capability assessment with auditable evidence and scoring. The page says DCAM is available exclusively to member firms.
practical_examples: None public beyond structure counts.
why_it_matters: Establishes what can be cited publicly: structure only.
authority_rationale: Owner's marketing page; framework text is members only.
notes: Names of the eight components were not captured from the text.

title: ISO/IEC 25012 data quality model summary
engineering_principles: Definitions of all 15 characteristics, grouped as inherent, both, and system-dependent.
practical_examples: Traceability defined around an audit trail of access and changes.
why_it_matters: Resolves the gap on the list of characteristics, from a secondary site.
authority_rationale: Secondary portal, not ISO; wording may differ from the standard.
notes: Paginated with ?start=N; pages 0 to 14 were opened to obtain all 15 definitions.

title: ISO 8000 (Wikipedia list of parts)
engineering_principles: Lists parts including 8000-2, 8000-8, 8000-61 and the 8000-1xx master data parts.
practical_examples: ISO 8000-150:2022 roles and responsibilities; ISO 8000-110:2021 master data exchange.
why_it_matters: Only opened inventory of parts; ISO's own pages returned 403.
authority_rationale: Community reference. Use for orientation only.
notes: https://eccma.org/what-is-iso-8000/ was also opened. No free official ISO 8000 part was found.

title: Documenting Architecture Decisions
engineering_principles: Records context, decision, status and consequences, because past rationale otherwise gets lost.
practical_examples: AWS guidance adds owner, Proposed, Accepted and Rejected states and supersession.
why_it_matters: Origin of the common ADR format, applicable to schema decisions.
authority_rationale: Widely referenced original post, read directly.
notes: Also opened: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/architectural-decision-records/adr-process.html and https://adr.github.io/. Data dictionary support via https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-comment.html (opened).
